title: Form 16 for ITR Filing 2026: Your Guide to Job Switches
description: Form 16 is a crucial document for salaried individuals to file their Income Tax Return (ITR) for FY 2025-26. Your employer is legally mandated to issue Form 1.

faq.q: What if my employer doesn't issue Form 16 by the deadline?
faq.a: If your employer fails to issue Form 16 by June 15, 2026, you should first follow up with them. If it's still not issued, you can use your payslips, bank statements, and Form 26AS/AIS to file your ITR, as these documents also contain income and TDS details.

faq.q: Is Form 16 mandatory for filing ITR?
faq.a: While Form 16 greatly simplifies ITR filing for salaried individuals, it is not strictly mandatory if you have other documents to substantiate your income and TDS. You can use payslips, bank statements, and Form 26AS/AIS as alternatives.

faq.q: What should I do if there are errors in my Form 16?
faq.a: If you find any discrepancies in your Form 16, immediately inform your employer. They are required to issue a revised Form 16 after making the necessary corrections. Ensure the revised document is also downloaded from the TRACES portal.

faq.q: Can I file ITR without Form 16 if I have only one employer?
faq.a: Yes, you technically can, but it is highly advisable to obtain Form 16. Without it, you would need to manually calculate your taxable income and deductions, which increases the chance of errors and potential scrutiny from the Income Tax Department.

faq.q: What if I had multiple employers and one of them is now closed?
faq.a: If a previous employer has closed down and cannot issue Form 16, you must rely on your payslips, bank statements, and particularly your Form 26AS/AIS for that period. These government-maintained records will show the TDS deducted by the closed entity.

faq.q: Do I need to report income from other sources (e.g., freelancing, interest) if I have Form 16?
faq.a: Yes, Form 16 only covers your salary income and TDS. You must report all other sources of income, such as interest from savings accounts, fixed deposits, capital gains, rental income, or any freelance earnings, in your ITR.

faq.q: How is Form 16 different from Form 16A?
faq.a: Form 16 is for tax deducted on salary income. Form 16A is for TDS on non-salary income, such as interest income from fixed deposits, professional fees, or rent. Both are TDS certificates, but for different types of income.
